citations.evidenceText:
Fuzzification:
•   Fuzzification is the process of converting input and output values into their
   membership functions.
•  The result of fuzzification is a set of graphs or equations that describe the
   degree of membership of different values in different fuzzy variables.
•  To fuzzify a variable, its range of possible values is divided into a number of sets,
   each describing a particular portion of the range.
•  Then each range is represented by an equation or a graph that describes the
   degree of truth or membership of each value within the range.
•  The number of sets, the range that each set represents,
   and the type of representation is arbitrary and a choice
   of the designer of the system.
•  These can be modified and improved when the system
    is simulated and analyzed.

citations.evidenceText:
Fuzzy Inference Rule Base

•  Fuzzy Inference Rule Base is the controller part of the system and is based on
   truth table logic.
•  The rule base is a collection of rules related to the fuzzy sets, the input
   variables, and the output variables and is meant to allow the system to decide
   what to do in each case.
•   It generally takes one of the following forms, depending on the number of input

Fuzzy Inference Rule Base

•  Fuzzy Inference Rule Base is the controller part of the system and is based on

concepts.title: Linguistic descriptors

concepts.title: Crisp thermostat threshold
concepts.description: The shown comparison has a sharp inclusive threshold; hysteresis and graded control are not specified.

concepts.title: Fuzzy-control stages
concepts.description: The stages encode linguistic inputs, apply control rules and convert the inferred output into an actionable value.

concepts.title: Foundational attribution
concepts.description: The slide explicitly credits Lotfi Zadeh; it does not provide a publication year.

concepts.title: Crisp value versus label
concepts.description: A crisp numerical input can be evaluated against several fuzzy labels without ceasing to be a definite measurement.

concepts.title: Crisp membership is not singleton-only
concepts.description: A crisp singleton is one particular set. General crisp sets can contain many values while retaining binary membership.

concepts.title: Interpreting a membership grade
concepts.description: Membership lies in [0,1] and expresses degree of belonging under the chosen definition, not an automatic probability.

concepts.title: Designing a function versus evaluating it
concepts.description: The source’s broad design-stage wording should be separated from runtime evaluation of already defined membership functions.
concepts.subtopic: Designing a function versus evaluating it

concepts.title: Design freedom and validation
concepts.description: Membership design is adjustable and should be analyzed rather than assumed correct.

concepts.title: Gaussian and trapezoidal shapes
concepts.description: The trapezoid uses simple line equations and four breakpoints; it may approximate a bell without being identical.

concepts.title: Trapezoidal interpolation
concepts.description: At x=8 the membership is halfway down the final line segment.

concepts.title: Triangular interpolation
concepts.description: The two straight-line ramps are symmetric about x=5.

concepts.title: S and Z shoulders
concepts.description: Shoulders can hold membership at 0 or 1 over an input range; a vertical-sided trapezoid is a simplified model, not necessarily the same smooth curve.

concepts.title: Gaussian membership versus density
concepts.description: The supplied Gaussian membership is dimensionless and unit-height; it is not a normalized probability density.

concepts.title: Antecedents and consequents
concepts.description: Rules connect input-label conditions to output-label consequences; the lecture also permits combined conditions and multiple consequences.

concepts.title: Specified fuzzy operators
concepts.description: The selected min/max conventions are common choices; AND is not universally forced to be minimum in every fuzzy system.

concepts.title: Singleton weighted average
concepts.description: The crisp output is a normalized weighted combination of singleton values, retaining the output’s physical units.

concepts.title: Zero total activation
concepts.description: A no-fire input requires a specified design response; silently inventing an output hides a coverage gap.

concepts.title: Mamdani pipeline
concepts.description: The area centroid depends on the consolidated output shape, not solely on the locations of its original peaks.

concepts.title: Clipping versus scaling
concepts.description: Clipping caps a consequent at the rule strength; scaling by multiplication is a different implication choice.

concepts.title: Maximum aggregation
concepts.description: Maximum aggregation forms an upper envelope and does not double-count overlap as ordinary addition.

concepts.title: Singleton weights versus area centroid
concepts.description: Keep the output representation and aggregation method explicit before comparing numerical answers.

concepts.title: Cooling-controller variables
concepts.description: The controller maps measured environmental conditions to a power-setting command, not directly to a guaranteed room temperature.

concepts.title: Cooling rule-grid size
concepts.description: The 12-rule base covers the pairwise combinations; choosing one consequent for each pair does not multiply the number of antecedent pairs.

concepts.title: Temperature-overlap geometry
concepts.description: The overlapping triangles can assign partial membership to both labels for the same crisp temperature.

concepts.title: Reported grade versus exact interpolation
concepts.description: Linear interpolation gives (78−75)/(85−75)=0.30. The source states 0.27 for its worked example; calculations using that example must label it as a supplied grade.

concepts.title: Descending humidity axis and interpolation
concepts.description: The descending plot axis does not change the numeric interpolation: μ_Humid(70)=20/30. The separately printed 0.65 is an approximate or separately supplied example value.

concepts.title: Reading the reversed power axis
concepts.description: The plotted orientation is reversed, but the power values remain 20 for Slow and 50 for Medium.

concepts.title: Complete cooling-rule pattern
concepts.description: Humidity affects several temperature rows; neither temperature nor humidity alone determines every consequent.

concepts.title: Tracing the active rules
concepts.description: The rule-network paths and minimum operation give Medium 0.27 and Slow 0.65; partial diagram wiring does not remove the other written rules.

concepts.title: Overlapping memberships need not sum to one
concepts.description: Membership degrees of different linguistic sets are not automatically probabilities of mutually exclusive events.
concepts.subtopic: Overlapping memberships need not sum to one

concepts.title: Cooling singleton calculation
concepts.description: The weighted singleton output is (0.65×20+0.27×50)/(0.65+0.27)=1325/46≈28.8043%, which rounds to the source’s 29%.

concepts.title: Reconstructing the clipped-area centroid
concepts.description: The explicit clipped-triangle reconstruction has area 2403/80 and first moment 2429293/2400, giving centroid 2429293/72090≈33.6981%. This supports the reported rounded 34% without pretending to recover unprovided simulation code.

concepts.title: Common weight scaling
concepts.description: Only relative weights matter for this normalized singleton average when the total remains positive; the same claim is not automatically true for clipped-area shapes.
